extracted.intended_audience: Inventors, plant breeders, botanists, and entrepreneurs seeking to file a U.S. plant patent
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for preparing and filing a plant patent application in the United States (35 U.S.C. §161 and USPTO rules), including eligibility, patentability, specification content, claim limits, and filing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine Inventorship (Ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who actually invented the new plant; an inventor is an 'individual(s) who invented or discovered the subject matter of the invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship can include more than one person — contributing to the creation or discovery (not merely reproducing the plant) is required to be a co-inventor. Inventors are listed on the application data and publication (order shown as on the application). Verify and document correct inventorship before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Patent Eligibility (statutory definition, 35 U.S.C. 161)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbatim statutory test: 'Whoever invents or discovers and asexually reproduces any distinct and new variety of plant, including cultivated sports, mutants, hybrids, and newly found seedlings, other than a tuber propagated plant or a plant found in an uncultivated state, may obtain a patent therefor...' (35 USC 161).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify the plant must be: (1) invented or discovered, (2) asexually reproduced, (3) distinct and new, and (4) not a tuber-propagated plant nor found in an uncultivated state. Use USPTO guidance and model after existing granted plant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asexual Reproduction Requirement (what asexually reproduced means and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asexual reproduction means the plant grows without fertilized seeds; reproduced without sexual fertilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of asexual reproduction methods include rooting cuttings, grafting and budding, apomictic seeds, bulbs, division, slips, layering, rhizomes, runners, corms, tissue culture, and nucellar embryos. Ensure method used qualifies as asexual reproduction for plant patent eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible Plants: tuber-propagated plants and plants found in an uncultivated state; alternative protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuber-propagated plants (e.g., potato, onion) and plants found in an uncultivated state are excluded from plant patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For seed-based or tuber plants, consider Plant Variety Protection Office (PVPO) certificates (PVPA) as an alternative. Utility patents may be available for new cultivation methods, genes (GMO), or devices related to plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability substantive criteria (eligible, no prior public use/sale, novel, non-obvious)
rubrics_metrics.description: For allowance an examiner must see the plant is eligible and meets novelty and nonobviousness requirements and is not barred by prior public use or sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements spelled out: Eligible (per step 2), No prior public use or sale (not patented, on sale, publicly used before effective filing date), Novel (differs from known related plants by at least one distinguishing characteristic beyond growing-condition differences), Non-obvious (would not have been obvious to one having ordinary skill in the art as of effective filing date). Perform novelty/nonobviousness searches similar to utility/design searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filing prerequisite — Discovery step (how the novel plant may be identified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before filing, the inventor must discover or identify a novel plant by acceptable means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable discovery situations include: grown in any cultivated area; occurring in a monoculture or known variety; a desirable mutant (spontaneous or induced); recognized as an outstanding single outlier within progeny from a planned breeding program. Document discovery evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filing prerequisite — Asexual reproduction testing and stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Must asexually reproduce the plant and test stability to confirm unique characteristics are stable and not transitory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test stability by propagating clones of the same genotype and analyzing each closely to confirm the unique characteristics are present and not caused by disease, infection, or other transitory changes. Record propagation tests and results to support the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification requirement per 37 C.F.R. §1.163(a): full botanical description and distinguishing characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Title 37 CFR 1.163(a) requires the specification 'must contain as full and complete a botanical description as reasonably possible of the plant and the characteristics which distinguish that plant over known, related plants.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification must be botanical in nature and sufficiently detailed to prevent later applicants from obtaining a patent by simply adding more detail. Use botanical terms and describe all distinguishing characteristics substantively even if depicted in photos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Title of the invention may include an introductory portion stating the name, citizenship, and residence of the inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the chosen plant name (varietal denomination) is not already taken; search UPOV or similar registries to avoid duplicative varietal names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Related Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Related applications may include utility applications from which the plant is a divisional, continuations, or copending applications to siblings or similar plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose related applications and relationships (co-pending, continuation, divisional, non-co-pending earlier applications) as applicable in the application paperwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Latin name and varietal denomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the Latin name of the genus and species of the plant claimed as well as the varietal denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate botanical identification using accepted Latin genus/species names and a clear varietal denomination for the claimed cultivar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is a short description that can be understood by a lay person; it describes the plant generally and includes the most notable or novel and important characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the abstract concise and accessible to non-specialists while highlighting novel/important functionality or characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Background includes the field of invention and a description of the relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the technical field and summarize prior related plants/techniques to contextualize the novelty and advantages of the claimed plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary describes key functionalities and characteristics of the plant and how it differentiates from others in the same species and class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative or lists to spell out distinguishing characteristics and consumer (or practical) benefits of the plant relative to related varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Brief Description of the Drawings/Photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural language explanation of what is shown in drawings or photos, including perspective, angle, partial or complete views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe photos/drawings clearly and link illustrations to claimed distinguishing features; note whether views are partial or complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required specification sections: Detailed Botanical Description (content elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete botanical description of the claimed plant is required, covering numerous plant parts and characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail items that should be included: genus and species; habit of growth; cultivar name; precocity; botanical characteristics of plant structures (buds, bark, foliage, flowers, fruit, etc.); fertility/fecundity; other distinguishing features such as disease resistance, drought/cold tolerance, fragrance, color, timing of flowering, productivity, rooting ability, extract quality, etc. Describe characteristics in botanical terms and provide substantive detail even for features shown in photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting constraints for plant patents (ONE claim only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patents get only one claim; 'You only get ONE claim!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The single claim must be a single sentence in formal language covering the plant 'as shown and described' and the language should be drawn to the plant as a whole. Clauses should point out and distinctly claim the unusual characteristics. Do not claim parts or products of the plant. Claim drafting is specialized — consider a patent attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and photographs requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings/photographs must showcase the most distinctive and novel features; photographs are required in many cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations must show whatever is stated in the claim language and be no smaller than 50% to scale of the actual plant. Photographs are required for plant patents; color photographs are required if one of the claimed features deals with color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing procedure and practical filing advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a plant patent application follows the same procedures as a utility application; USPTO incentivizes electronic filing by charging a lower fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use electronic filing for lower fees and consult USPTO for current submission requirements. Ensure all prerequisite observations/tests are complete before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation and evidence retention requirement before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, all parts of the plant should be thoroughly observed for at least one growth cycle and any observations or findings should be recorded and submitted with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain detailed records of observations across a growth cycle; include propagation data, photographs, and test results to support stability and distinguishing characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model application format on a granted plant patent (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO tip: if drafting your first plant patent application, model the application after one that has already been granted; use the same or similar format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine granted plant patents (examples given such as PP27,475) to follow successful formatting, sectioning, and disclosure depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider hiring a patent attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: you really shouldn't file a plant (or any) patent application on your own — hire a professional patent attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the person is a registered patent attorney (look them up in USPTO registry). The attorney can assist with inventorship, claim drafting, ensuring the specification meets 37 CFR 1.163(a), handling related applications, and overall prosecution strategy.
